mechanism: Ultra-long-acting, fully biased GLP-1 receptor agonist administered by subcutaneous injection. Pfizer lists berobenatide (MET-097i; PF-08653944) as a Phase 3 biologic for chronic weight management, and the assigned VESPER-5 trial describes MET097 as a fully biased ultra-long-acting GLP-1RA.
development_status: Recruiting Phase 3 VESPER-5 trial in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, with 999 planned participants, weekly subcutaneous PF-08653944 versus placebo, and Week 64 percent body-weight change as the primary endpoint. Related VESPER-4 Phase 3 trial in obesity/overweight without T2D is also recruiting, and VESPER-3 Phase 2b has company-reported positive topline monthly-maintenance data.
clinical_summary: PF-08653944 is positioned as a long-acting GLP-1 asset with weekly and monthly development paths. The assigned VESPER-5 Phase 3 study targets obesity/overweight with T2D and measures body weight, HbA1c, cardiometabolic lipids, blood pressure, and categorical weight-loss thresholds through Weeks 64 and 84. Pfizer reported VESPER-3 met its Week 28 primary endpoint with up to 12.3% mean placebo-adjusted weight loss after weekly dosing through Week 12 followed by monthly dosing, with no plateau observed at Week 28. Differentiation depends on whether Phase 3 confirms competitive efficacy and better convenience than weekly GLP-1/GIP analogs.
safety_summary: No posted ClinicalTrials.gov results are available for VESPER-5, VESPER-4, or VESPER-3. Pfizer reported VESPER-3 GI TEAEs were predominantly mild or moderate through Week 28, with limited severe nausea/vomiting, no severe diarrhea, and treatment discontinuations due to AEs in active arms but not placebo. GLP-1 class analog monitoring should include GI intolerance, dehydration/acute kidney injury, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, hypoglycemia risk with insulin or insulin secretagogues, diabetic retinopathy in T2D, delayed gastric emptying/oral drug absorption, aspiration risk around anesthesia, hypersensitivity, pregnancy avoidance, and contraindication/precaution logic around medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2.
management_tools: Prior authorization requiring FDA-labeled obesity or overweight criteria and documentation of baseline BMI
Require type 2 diabetes or weight-related comorbidity where aligned to final indication and plan benefit design
Document reduced-calorie diet, increased physical activity, and behavioral modification participation
Quantity limits aligned to final weekly or monthly labeled dose and device presentation
No concurrent use with other GLP-1, GLP-1/GIP, or incretin weight-management agents
Continuation criteria tied to clinically meaningful weight loss, HbA1c improvement in T2D, tolerability, and adherence
Step therapy or preferred sequencing against covered semaglutide, tirzepatide, or other preferred anti-obesity agents where contractually and clinically appropriate

Safety screening for personal or family history of MTC/MEN2, pancreatitis or gallbladder history, severe GI disease/gastroparesis, pregnancy plans, diabetic retinopathy, and hypoglycemia risk with insulin or sulfonylureas
Reauthorization intervals requiring current weight, percent weight change from baseline, cardiometabolic response, and ongoing lifestyle intervention
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for the assigned VESPER-5 Phase 3 study.
VESPER-5 primary completion is estimated for 2027-10-12 and study completion for 2028-05-16.
Company-reported VESPER-3 data are topline; detailed results were announced for presentation after the current check date.
Final approved dose, weekly versus monthly commercial positioning, label scope, and U.S. launch timing are not yet established.
No direct U.S. price exists; annual cost is derived from GLP-1 obesity analogs and public pricing anchors.

sources.title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine (PF-08653944) in People With Obesity or Overweight and Type 2 Diabetes (T2D)
supports: Official title identifies VESPER-5 as a Phase 3 multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial of MET097, a fully biased ultra-long-acting GLP-1RA, in people with overweight or obesity and T2D
Sponsor is Pfizer and overall status is recruiting
Estimated enrollment is 999 participants with actual start date 2026-02-24, estimated primary completion 2027-10-12, and estimated study completion 2028-05-16
Intervention is subcutaneous PF-08653944, also named MET097, versus placebo
Primary endpoint is percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 64

Secondary endpoints include body-weight change, HbA1c change, at least 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% body-weight reduction, triglycerides, non-HDL-C, and other cardiometabolic outcomes through Weeks 64 and 84
ClinicalTrials.gov states the study is FDA-regulated as a drug study and no results are posted

Primary endpoint is percent change from baseline in body weight at Week 64
Secondary endpoints include at least 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% weight reduction, triglycerides, non-HDL-C, systolic blood pressure, and physical function

sources.title: Pfizer's Ultra-Long-Acting Injectable GLP-1 RA Shows Robust and Continued Weight Loss with Monthly Dosing in Phase 2b Trial
supports: Pfizer identifies PF-08653944 as PF'3944, previously MET-097i, an investigational fully biased ultra-long-acting injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist
Company reported VESPER-3 met the primary endpoint of statistically significant weight reduction at Week 28 across all four dose regimens versus placebo

sources.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) Prescribing Information
supports: Zepbound is a GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist indicated with reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for adult chronic weight reduction and maintenance in obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity
Label includes boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors and contraindication for personal or family history of MTC or MEN2

Warnings include severe GI adverse reactions, acute kidney injury due to volume depletion, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, hypersensitivity, hypoglycemia with insulin or insulin secretagogues, diabetic retinopathy, and pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia/deep sedation

Most common adverse reactions include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, injection-site reactions, fatigue, hypersensitivity reactions, eructation, hair loss, and GERD
Zepbound delays gastric emptying and can affect absorption of oral medications

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from recruiting Phase 3 obesity program, VESPER-4 and VESPER-5 primary completions in September-October 2027, study completions in April-May 2028, and expected time for full Phase 3 package completion, filing, review, and launch preparation.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A first U.S. obesity launch before 2029 is unlikely because pivotal studies are ongoing with no posted results, but Pfizer's active Phase 3 program and public acquisition milestones support a plausible 2029-2031 launch window if Phase 3 efficacy and safety are positive.

annual_cost_range.method: Used public obesity GLP-1 analog pricing. Low equals Wegovy post-offer self-pay pen price of $349 per month multiplied by 12. High equals Zepbound pen WAC of $1,086.37 per four-pen pack multiplied by 12 and rounded to the nearest dollar.
annual_cost_range.explanation: PF-08653944 is unapproved and unpriced. A public analog range anchored by current GLP-1 direct/cash and WAC prices gives a conservative planning range before rebates, discounts, adherence effects, device differences, or final weekly/monthly launch pricing.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted Phase 3 status, long-acting fully biased GLP-1 mechanism, monthly-maintenance development, company-reported VESPER-3 efficacy/tolerability, and large pivotal program against lack of posted Phase 3 results and crowded GLP-1/GIP competition.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Potential monthly dosing is meaningfully differentiated if Phase 3 confirms weight loss, T2D metabolic benefit, and tolerability. Current evidence remains below high differentiation because VESPER-3 is topline and approved weekly competitors already have strong efficacy and outcomes footprints.

budget_impact.method: Combined chronic use in a high-prevalence obesity/T2D population, current GLP-1 analog annual costs, and payer policy evidence showing PA, continuation, and class-combination controls are already needed for covered GLP-1 obesity products.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if priced competitively, broad obesity and T2D eligibility can create high aggregate plan spend; utilization controls and benefit-design exclusions are likely central to management.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed Phase 3 program breadth, Pfizer commercial scale, potential monthly dosing, company-reported VESPER-3 efficacy/tolerability, and active obesity/T2D positioning against entrenched semaglutide/tirzepatide competitors.
disruption_risk.explanation: A long-acting GLP-1 with monthly optionality could disrupt formulary contracting, adherence assumptions, GLP-1 sequencing, and access policy if pivotal outcomes confirm competitive efficacy and safety.

recommended_action.method: Mapped recruiting Phase 3 status, high-budget category, potential monthly dosing differentiation, and 2029-2031 derived launch window to early active planning rather than passive monitoring.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin scenario planning for formulary placement, PA/continuation criteria, step sequencing, quantity limits, and contracting assumptions while monitoring VESPER-4/VESPER-5 readouts and monthly VESPER-6 development.
